turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Good morning, come in and have a seat. How has your week been feeling since we last spoke?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: A bit mixed, honestly. Some days were okay, but other times my mind has been in a pretty heavy place.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: What's been sitting with you the most over the past few days?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Living in this shared apartment with three roommates, I’ve never felt more isolated. They cook dinner together, watch shows in the living room, and I just sit in my dark bedroom with headphones on. It's like I'm a ghost haunting the hallway. I just don't belong anywhere, not with them, not with anyone.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Feeling like a ghost in your own living space is such a disorienting, isolating feeling. It sounds like there's been a very heavy wall between you and them.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yeah, it's just been sitting heavily with me. Though I have been trying to stick to my day-to-day routine as best as I can.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: How have your energy levels been throughout the mornings this week?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: A bit groggy at first, but once I get that first cup of black coffee down, I start easing into the routine.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: That makes sense. Have you been able to maintain a regular bedtime schedule?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Mostly around eleven. Some nights I read a chapter of my book, other nights I just turn the lights out right away.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: What kind of book are you reading currently?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: It's a historical biography about early polar expeditions. It's surprisingly engaging.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: That sounds intriguing. Did you manage to take any brief walks during your lunch breaks?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I walked over to the park near the office on Tuesday and Wednesday. The autumn breeze was actually really refreshing.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Noticing physical sensations like the breeze is a great grounding exercise. How was work otherwise?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: A lot of administrative backlog. We had a systems migration, so half the morning was just fixing broken spreadsheet formulas.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: It sounds like you've been navigating the daily grind as best as you can. How are you feeling right now in this room?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I'm still feeling like a total ghost in that apartment. Even last night when I walked into the kitchen for water, nobody looked up or said a word. That barrier is very real and I just do not fit in with them or anyone else.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Walking into that silence felt like another confirmation of that barrier. I hear how exhausting that ongoing disconnection is.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: It is. It makes me want to withdraw even deeper into my room.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Thank you for being so honest about how deeply that pain is still present. Let's make sure you take gentle care of yourself this afternoon.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I'll try to just rest. Thank you for listening.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: You're very welcome. We will pick this right back up next week.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: See you next week.
